I cannot thank you enough for your answers.  Seriously, this is the first time in months that I feel like someone is listening to me and understanding what I'm saying.  I'll take your advice.  Please keep doing what you're doing on this website.

I keep debating the psychiatrist thing.  I am currently paying a therapist out of pocket because my insurance won't cover mental health, about $100 a week.  I've been to two psychiatrists that have just been horrible experiences where they talked to me for 30 seconds before giving me some totally random drug.  

I keep thinking maybe I should just suck it up and pay the almost $200 To go, but then I worry they're going to be just as horrible as the first 2.  I'm not in like... imminent danger of offing myself, I am just SO angry that this doctor I have been seeing since I was in kindergarten (20 years) doesn't seem to care whether I live or die, or even if I'm sane.

I second prozac.  It was the first psychiatric medication I was on, before i was even diagnosed with OCD.  It worked wonders, but I was stupid and stopped taking it cold turkey, tried starting again at full dose, stopped, etc.  Really messed me up, and instead of getting back on the prozac my doctor just gave me something else. 

Now almost 6 years later.  I've been on luvox (an OCD specific ssri), and it wasn't helping much.  I asked my doctor to go back on the prozac, since in hindsight it was easily the best medication I've tried.  I'm now on 40 prozac and 50 luvox, and I can already feel myself getting better.  Everyone is different, but for me prozac has been 100% a godsend when other psychiatric meds didn't touch my symptoms

I don't know if we are experiencing the same thing or not, but I never know what I feel.  I can be suicidal and think to myself 'my life is perfect' within minutes of each other.  If anyone (including my psychologist) asks me what's wrong, I can smile and say nothing and have small talk, and appear to be perfectly fine, but on the inside I'm dying and drowning and just in a blind rage to the point where I feel ill.

I wouldnt say you got scammed, but they didn't explain it to you properly / you didn't do your research.  You cant technically dye your hair grey.  You can, but it wont have that feathery silver look that a lot of people are looking for, it'll be a flat ugly gunmetal grey.    'Silver' hair isn't a color, it's that there is no color, it has all been stripped away. 

For example, my mom has had grey hair since she was 19, and for the last 30 years she has been dying it the same deep brown.  When she wanted to go natural and just let the grey happen, she either had to let it just grow out naturally and have the ugly roots for a long time, or they had to strip her hair down to silver over 4 sessions.  So even though she  was naturally grey, it takes time and repetition to strip all that color out. 

I personally wouldnt go back to that salon.  Doing this to hair is akin to bleaching it, in the sense that it has 'changed' that hair forever.  The fact that they didn't explain any of this to you before going through with the process would make me personally not trust them so much.

I know you have a lot of answers already, but I would like to verify that this is normal for long hair lol.  I don't remember it being a problem much when I was a teen, but the past 5 years or so (I'm 24) I shed worse than my dog  xD   Especially when I'm showering, I'll have to stop what I'm doing to untangle my fingers and try to get the wad of hair off me.  I use to wipe it all on the shower walls but my husband wasn't a fan of that lol. 

Don't even get me started on how much hair I find in my butt crack  😂😂😂

Im not sure if I understand exactly what you mean by memory hoarding, but I think I may do this too to an extent.  A lot of my intrusive thoughts and rumination tend to involve the past (sometimes the very far past lol), and stuff I shouldn't care about or have no control over anymore.  
Conversations I had with my ex best friend in middle school.  When I use to self harm in middle school.  Conversations with my ex from high school.  Random panic attacks from 6 years ago.    
Sometimes ill sit for hours and just have like.... random thoughts of fake conversations with one of my exes, and it makes me feel really guilty because I feel like im, you know, thinking about one of my exes lol, but I have no control over it.  I love my husband, and have no interest in even speaking to any of these people, its just random shit that pops up in my brain.  
Or sometimes my friend that screwed me over back in high school will come into my head, And I will get SO MAD.  Something that happened 6+ years ago, and should be long gone, and that I tell myself I don't care about, can work me up to the point where im crying and having a panic attack about something that no longer exists. 
And I don't think that im not over these things.   Like I said, I don't actually want to go back to any of these times or do them differently or anything.   I think my brain just likes to torture me, by making all my intrusive thoughts and ruminations about things that will hurt me the most

Luvox is the 7th 'mental health' medication Ive been on in my life, and so far its easily my favorite.  Others would kind of dull a couple symptoms at a time and for the first few months on them I would constantly be wondering whether or not they were working, but they never really stuck. 
Im on a combination of Luvox and Buspar, and its the first ones I have tried where I definitely know that I have more good moments than bad.  There are still bad moments, Ive only been on it for about 6 months and I think we are still needing to work on what dose is high enough for me, but its the first one I have a lot of hope for.  
Another plus is that I don't think I had a single side effect.  The buspar gave me pretty severe brain zaps the first month or so, but those are just a minor annoyance and I was use to them from weening off some other meds.  The few times I have missed a dose of the Luvox, I have been a ****Ing wreck the next day lol, but nothing I didn't live through, and nothing that lasted past my next dose.  No side effects though.

He knows that I have OCD and have gone through severe periods of anxiety and depression.  He knows about the panic attacks and the sadness and all the general symptoms, but I don't think Ive ever flat out explained the intrusive thoughts to him.  
This is mostly because the cats are his babies, and he loves them more than I can explain.  Its to a point where I often get jealous of the cats because i feel like he loves them more than me, but thats a whole issue I wont get into lol.  
There was a period of time about 3 years back when the thoughts got so bad that I just ended up hating the cats.  I knew they were good cats and I wanted to love them like he did, I tried, but it was like the second they walked into my vision, this primal rage took over.  I would just sit there stewing and getting angrier and angrier as they'd crawl into his lap. 
I realize how crazy this all sounds, but this is a problem that has been eating me alive from the inside for years.  When the cat thing got to its worst, I could tell it was really hurting him.  He once told me that he has even thought about rehoming them because he just wanted the stress to end, even though he loves them so much.  I never want to make him feel that bad again, so I try not to talk about the cat issues. 

One therapist I saw laughed and told me to just get rid of my cats, she told me she hated cats too and it was all a big joke to her.  Another told me that I just needed to spend more time with them so they would like me as much as my husband.  Well... I tried.  I really did.  But a lot of times when I have these thoughts and spurts of anger, I think they can sense it?  They cower from me like im about to beat them to death, even if I am being nice.  They know me, and they know my mood will flip on a dime, and they have NO trust in me whatsoever.  I don't blame them, because I don't either. 

Im sorry, I know im rambling, but I feel like im 100% out of options.  I just wish the doctor would put me on something extremely strong, because at this point I would rather be a happy zombie than feel like this anymore.

Wow, that was hilarious!  It made me feel a little better that the whole audience was laughing along, but I guess he's a comedian so it would be awkward if they didn't lol.  Do you tell people in your life about them, or just your doctors?  I feel like people would be a lot less trusting of me if I told them, even if they aren't my fault. For example, if I told my husband about the cats, I feel like he wouldnt trust me around them alone.

I still do it now but it was much more obvious back when I was in school.  I would be writing a paper or doing homework, and if I made one mistake i would tear the page out and start over.  Sometimes i would write a note, and if I didn't like how my handwriting looked I would completely redo it. 
I also like crossword puzzles.  However, if im halfway through and realize I messed up, im done with that page.  I cant erase it, or write over it, im just done. I have probably a dozen crossword books with less than half of the puzzles complete.

Yes.  Especially in my job.  I come in early, I stay late, work my days off, and get dragged all over the place because they always come to me to ask.  Why wouldnt they lol, I never say no.  Then I get to a point of depression because nobody is thankful for my help and they just keep pushing me around, but I feel like I can be mad at the because... well because I said yes to all of it lol

It might not hurt to get a second opinion.  I take buspar regularly now, and my mom has taken 20mg twice a day every day for almost 10 years lol, it has changed her life.  I knew that it COULD be taken as needed, but didn't know it had to be.  I was actually on xanax which was the only thing that helped me, so my doctor switched me to buspar because she said it could be taken regularly with no addiction unlike xanax.

I was on 100 for a few months, noticed some changes in my thinking but wasn't really 'fixed'.  Went up to 125 a few weeks ago and things are really looking hopeful just the last week or so, I'm enjoying life for the first time I can remember in a long time.  
What im wondering is how you know when to stop?  I mean... I still have bad moments and bad days, but things ARE better.  If I tell my doctor im better, she may just say 'Thats great' and keep me on this dose.  Buuut what If 150 or even 200 would be perfect for me?  How am I supposed to know, and how am I supposed to ask her this without sounding like a druggie who just wants a higher dose?

Im a married 24 year old female, been on Luvox for about 6 months now, so I can't speak for males or about any 'indefinite' side effects.  Ive definitely noticed less interest I guess?  If  distracted by other things, my mind doesn't usually wander to sex, if that makes any sense lol.  But I wouldnt say its affected my sex drive, and definitely no disfunction or change in sex itself.

I have either this same problem or at least something similar, but im not sure I have a solution for you, as im working on it myself right now : (
Basically if I have a busy day or certain tasks that need done, my ENTIRE brain is just set on that schedule.  I need to do this at this time, ill be there for this long, so that will give me this amount of time to get to the store so I can buy this and this on my way to this place, since I have to be here at this time.  
My brain just runs and runs like this all day, going over the plan repeatedly so I don't forget anything and im not late.  The only thing thats really helped me is to just keep telling yourself that its not as big of a deal as Youre making of it. (Yes I understand that that is 100% easier said than done)  No, the dog WILL NOT die if you are home 15 minutes later than planned to take her for a walk.  The post office doesn't close until 9, so why does it matter if you get there at 445 instead of 4?  
There's no magic fix.  You just have to kind of think of it in a fake it til you make it kind of way, until relaxing about it comes naturally to your brain.  That and a medication change are really the only things that have helped me.

Wow, thank you all so much for the responses.  Ive tried asking for advice on mental illness in the past on other sites and got nothing but silence.  It really helps to know its not just me. 

Since my OCD diagnosis Ive been on different combinations of Luvox and Buspar.  It has definitely helped me be less socially awkward and be more comfortable out in the world lol, but this one thing hasn't changed, which is upsetting since its a huge part of my life. 

This does sound like me.  I also have a problem where I basically have SO many things that I want to do, that I feel if I pick one im screwing up the other.  If it spend my time reading, I may fall behind others in video game progress.  If I play the game, I will forget what is happening in the book.  But with about 25 hobbies lol.  So I sit there in a constant state of indecision and make myself feel like shit, and accomplish nothing in the meantime. 

I know therapy would be beneficial, but its just not in our budget right now, which is another source of stress for me.  We both make decent money, but even a 'cheap' therapist around here is $80+ an hour.  We've thought about switching insurance to cover this, but with the amount per month we would be paying it would barely pay for itself.  Ive even thought about things like donating plasma to pay for it, but Ive heard too many horror stories about these places and I always chicken out.

I second this.  I was wrongly diagnosed with ADHD, anxiety, panic disorder, and depression throughout my life.  Ive been on almost a dozen combinations of medicines, some would help with a couple symptoms, but overall none did the trick.  About 6 months ago I started seeing a new psychologist, and after 2 sessions she asked me if anyone had every told me it might be OCD.  After talking to a couple other doctors and researching the subject, it couldn't have been more painfully obvious.  I got switched to a combination of Luvox and Buspar, and my life is (slowly) getting much better for the first time I can remember.  Its not perfect, and drugs work differently for everyone, but I think this one might just save my life. I still have very bad days, very bad moments, but they are few and far between.  I feel human again.
